comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, 85% of the home equity portfolio was in Consumer Banking, 10% in Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), and the remainder in All Other segments.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC explicitly identify 'All Other' as a specific portfolio segment within their reconciliation or distribution disclosures, distinguishing it from core operating segments like Consumer Banking. C discloses divestiture-related gains and expenses specifically within its 'All Other' segment, attributing $372 million in operating expenses to Mexico separation and Asia severance costs alongside gains from India and Taiwan sales. Similarly, BAC discloses the distribution of its home equity portfolio, noting that the remainder of the portfolio after allocating 85% to Consumer Banking and 10% to GWIM resides in 'All Other'. While C focuses on financial performance impacts (gains/expenses) within this segment and BAC focuses on asset composition, both disclosures use the 'All Other' classification to isolate items not reported in primary business lines.

sentences.text: (2) 2023 includes (i) an approximate $1.059 billion gain on sale recorded in revenue (approximately $727 million after-tax) related to the India consumer banking business sale; (ii) an approximate $403 million gain on sale recorded in revenue (approximately $284 million after-tax) related to the Taiwan consumer banking business sale; and (iii) approximately $372 million (approximately $263 million after-tax) in operating expenses, primarily related to separation costs in Mexico and severance costs in the Asia exit markets.
At December 31, 2024, 85 percent of the home equity portfolio was in Consumer Banking, 10 percent was in GWIM and the remainder of the portfolio was in All Other.
